synopsis: Rolling-wave planning is a schedule-planning method that details near-term work while outlining later work [f10099, f9586, f16271]. Chapter 12 recommends it on expert opinion and describes it as a high fit for situations combining high uncertainty with a fixed deadline [f10104, f10100]. The booklet attributes the method to PMI, and the glossary identifies the PMBOK Guide, seventh edition (2021), as a collection of accepted practices including rolling-wave planning [f10098, f16420]. Its status is documented practice rather than demonstrated effectiveness: the booklet found no supporting outcome evidence, but also found no evidence against it or identifying its limits [f10103, f16425, f10101, f10102].
